clue.text: A bit of a bore with money for wine

parts.note: the chamber is the part of a gun's bore that holds the cartridge
tin is old slang for cash

explanation.surface: A gun's barrel and some cash are swapped for a bottle of wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bore' suggests a tedious person, but it is the barrel of a gun.
explanation.definitionFit: Chambertin is a celebrated red Burgundy from the Côte de Nuits.

clue.text: Firm doctor appears to get shock under control

parts.note: CO is short for company, a firm
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's qualification

explanation.surface: A firm's doctor appears to bring a patient's shock under control.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shock' suggests medical shock, but it is a shock of hair.
explanation.definitionFit: Running teeth through untidy hair tames a shaggy mop.

clue.text: Silver ring on sea-bed

parts.note: Ag is the chemical symbol for silver
a ring is round in shape, a round

explanation.surface: A silver ring lies on the sea floor.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship stuck on the bottom in shallow water has run onto the bed.

clue.text: Book that's witty about pop music

parts.note: bright means clever or quick-witted
on means about, concerning
rock is a kind of popular music

explanation.surface: A clever book about pop music.
explanation.walkthrough: Brighton rock is also a British seaside candy stick, but here it is Graham Greene's novel.
explanation.definitionFit: Graham Greene's 1938 novel set among gangs in an English seaside town.

clue.text: Record organ part

definitions.meaning: a set of pipes controlled by a stop on a pipe organ

explanation.surface: Note down part of a church organ.
explanation.definitionFit: A register is both an official log and a stop or set of pipes on an organ.

clue.text: Home established and superficially decorated

parts.note: in means at home
laid means set down, as a foundation is laid

explanation.surface: A house is built and given a decorative finish.
explanation.definitionFit: Set into a surface as ornament, like marquetry pressed into wood.

clue.text: Lead of whom a member must follow?

definitions.text: Lead of whom a member must follow?

parts.words: Lead of whom a member must follow?
parts.note: in Parliament a party official tells each member how to vote, and members are expected to follow that lead

explanation.surface: A question about whose lead a club member has to follow.
explanation.walkthrough: In British politics the whip is the party officer who enforces voting discipline among MPs (members).
explanation.definitionFit: The party officer who instructs MPs how to vote is the person whose direction they must follow.

clue.text: Moorish cover girl

definitions.meaning: the plant that blankets upland moors

explanation.surface: A Moorish veil worn by a young woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Moorish' suggests the Moors of North Africa, but means belonging to a moor.
explanation.definitionFit: Ling covers British moorland, and it is also a woman's name.

clue.text: Blunt nib and paper without writing

parts.note: a nib is the point of a pen
a blank sheet has nothing written on it

explanation.surface: A dull nib and an empty sheet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blunt' reads as describing the nib, but means frank.
explanation.definitionFit: Direct and frank, as a refusal given bluntly.

clue.text: Piece of harness that'll make better profit sooner or later

definitions.meaning: a strap running from the noseband or reins to the girth, keeping a horse's head down

definitions.text: that'll make better profit sooner or later
definitions.meaning: a gambling system of doubling the stake after each loss, which in theory must eventually show a gain

explanation.surface: A bit of horse tack promises a gambler eventual winnings.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a strap of horse tack and the doubling-up betting system that supposedly wins in the end.

clue.text: Garment is wrapped around artist's back

indicators.note: back tells us to read the whole assembled run in the opposite direction
the word is is split open so that it encloses the artist

parts.note: RA, Royal Academician, is the stock crossword artist

explanation.surface: Something is draped around a painter's back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back' looks like part of the artist's body, but it turns the whole assembly round; 'wrapped around' acts first. RA (Royal Academician) is the crossword's usual artist.
explanation.definitionFit: A sari is a long draped piece of cloth worn as a dress by women in South Asia.

clue.text: Favour including as weight valuable piece of basalt

indicators.note: including means the other letters are placed inside the favour

parts.note: a favour is a ribbon badge such as a rosette
a ton is a unit of weight

explanation.surface: A ribbon is given weight as a precious bit of rock.
explanation.walkthrough: A favour here is a ribbon worn to show support, such as at a horse show. The stone is in fact granodiorite, though long described as basalt.
explanation.definitionFit: The inscribed stele in the British Museum that unlocked Egyptian hieroglyphs is a slab of dark stone.

clue.text: To sell drugs illegally is offensive

definitions.meaning: to deal narcotics on the street
a military attack or big advance, as a noun

explanation.surface: Dealing narcotics is objectionable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'offensive' reads as an adjective (nasty) but is the noun meaning a military thrust.
explanation.definitionFit: Peddling drugs is slang for the verb, and a major attack or advance is the noun sense.

clue.text: Might it contain tot's head, and hair also?

definitions.text: Might it contain tot's head, and hair also?

indicators.note: the hat holds a jumble of these letters as well as a child's head, so the contents are mixed up

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

indicators.note: head means the first letter of the word tot's

explanation.surface: A question about whether a hat might hold a toddler's head and hair too.
explanation.walkthrough: An &lit: T (tot's head) with HAIR and ALSO is rearranged into the answer, and the whole clue describes the hat a child might wear.
explanation.definitionFit: A child's sailor-style cap sits on a little one's head, covering hair too.

clue.text: Valentine card given after piece of music's heard

indicators.note: given after places the card behind the sound-alike in the answer
heard means the word is replaced by one sounding the same

parts.note: a suite is an instrumental piece in several movements
a heart is a playing card of that suit

explanation.surface: A Valentine's card comes with a tune.
explanation.walkthrough: 'card' suggests a Valentine card, but it is a playing card.
explanation.definitionFit: A valentine is one's beloved, the person one woos on 14 February.

clue.text: Exposed liberal to public

parts.note: liberal in the sense of broad, generous, wide-ranging
public means open to everyone

explanation.surface: A liberal politician is exposed to public view.
explanation.definitionFit: Exposed and unprotected, as a goal left undefended or a position vulnerable to attack.

clue.text: Tree damaged, caught by wings of powerful bird

indicators.note: caught by means the scrambled tree sits inside the other letters
the wings of a word are its first and last letters
damaged means the letters of tree are broken up and rearranged

parts.note: fodder taken as written

explanation.surface: A tree is wrecked and seized by a mighty bird of prey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'powerful bird' looks like one phrase but 'powerful' only supplies its wings (first and last letters), and 'damaged' rearranges the tree into ETRE.
explanation.definitionFit: Petrels are seabirds, such as the storm petrel, that fly low over the ocean.

clue.text: Teacher putting mark one point up

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for the German mark
I is the Roman numeral one
to point up a matter is to emphasise or stress it

explanation.surface: A teacher marks one point higher.
explanation.walkthrough: 'point up' looks like adding a point to a grade, but means emphasise.
explanation.definitionFit: A schoolmistress is a female schoolteacher, an old-fashioned term.

clue.text: Heart led by opponents at bridge — play another!

parts.note: East and North are opponents at the bridge table, abbreviated E and N
the heart of something is its core

explanation.surface: A bridge player's heart lead prompts calls for another rubber.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heart' and 'led' suggest leading a card of the hearts suit at bridge, but heart is simply the centre; in bridge North and East sit as opponents.
explanation.definitionFit: The cry an audience shouts asking performers for one more number.

clue.text: Box around ring, only to be laid out on canvas later?

definitions.text: only to be laid out on canvas later?

indicators.note: around means the box encloses the ring

parts.note: a carton is a cardboard box
O resembles a ring

explanation.surface: A boxer in the ring is knocked out onto the canvas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Box', 'ring' and 'laid out on canvas' paint boxing, but the canvas is a painter's.
explanation.definitionFit: A full-size preparatory drawing that an artist transfers to a painting or tapestry.

clue.text: Within a short time, investment appears ill-judged

indicators.note: within means the investment is placed inside the other piece

parts.note: MIN is the short form of minute, itself a short time
a stake is money put into a venture

explanation.surface: An investment soon proves a bad call.
explanation.definitionFit: Wrong or misguided, as a judgement based on error.

clue.text: Small ruler used in making letters

indicators.note: used in means the answer is a run of letters found within the words that follow

explanation.surface: A small rule used for writing letters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ruler' looks like a measuring stick for lettering, but is a monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: A petty or minor king, of a small realm.

clue.text: Champ taken round one European city

indicators.note: taken round means the chewing word goes around the one

parts.note: to champ is to chew noisily, to munch
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A champion is taken on a tour of a European city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Champ' reads as champion, but is the verb meaning chew.
explanation.definitionFit: The Bavarian capital in southern Germany.

clue.text: No leniency here — for those involved with rackets?

definitions.text: No leniency here — for those involved with rackets?

parts.words: No leniency here — for those involved with rackets?
parts.note: reads as a strict law court for racketeers, but rackets are also tennis rackets, used on a surface like asphalt

explanation.surface: A tough tribunal awaits criminals who run rackets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rackets' suggests organised crime, but the tennis sense gives a non-grass playing surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A tennis surface of asphalt or concrete, while a stern tribunal would also be unyielding.

clue.text: Provide information linking gang-leader to offence

parts.note: a sin is a moral offence
the leading letter of gang is G

explanation.surface: An informer links a gang boss to a crime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gang-leader' suggests a crime boss, but it means just the first letter of 'gang'.
explanation.definitionFit: To inform on accomplices to the police, in criminal slang.

clue.text: Goose put in inferior oven without any stuffing

indicators.note: removing the stuffing leaves only the first and last letters of each word

explanation.surface: A goose is put in a poor oven without stuffing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Goose' and 'oven' suggest roasting, but a goose is a tailor's smoothing iron, named for its curved handle.
explanation.definitionFit: A tailor's goose is a heavy pressing tool with a gooseneck handle.

clue.text: It's a very old wicket, so declare

parts.note: W stands for wicket on a cricket scorecard

explanation.surface: An ancient cricket pitch prompts a captain to declare the innings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'declare' looks like a cricket captain ending an innings, fitting 'wicket', but it means state openly.
explanation.definitionFit: To state or affirm openly, as one professes a belief.

clue.text: Cold drink container English fan wanted after victory

indicators.note: after puts the English fan behind the victory in the answer

parts.note: a win is a victory
a fan is a device for cooling

explanation.surface: An English supporter wants a cold drink after a win.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fan' suggests a sports supporter, but it is a device that cools.
explanation.definitionFit: An ice bucket or chilling jacket that keeps bottles of chilled white at the right temperature.

clue.text: City, after half-time, barely extended

indicators.note: after puts the city behind the half-word in the answer
half of the hyphenated word time means its first two of four letters are kept

parts.note: NY is short for New York City

explanation.surface: A city side barely stretches their lead after the interval.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half-time' suggests a football interval, but it means half the letters of 'time'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something barely extended has scarcely any size, so it is minute.

clue.text: His father was a detective

parts.note: reads as a man whose parent was a police officer, but the father is the priest-sleuth Father Brown, created by this writer

explanation.surface: A man recalls that his dad worked as a detective.
explanation.walkthrough: G. K. Chesterton wrote the Father Brown stories, about a Catholic priest who solves crimes.
explanation.definitionFit: The English writer whose fictional priest Father Brown is an amateur sleuth.
